title: SQL executor, planner and correctness-first evolution
summary: Current SQL support includes substantial joins, set operations, correlated subqueries, aggregates, windows, recursive/multi CTEs, DML composition and planner access-path diagnostics. Equality may be an access-path optimisation rather than a grammar restriction; the complete predicate remains authoritative.
invariants: Malformed SQL and recognized-but-unsupported SQL remain distinct outcomes.
Never rewrite unsupported SQL into a different query.
Planner diagnostics such as accessPath and rowsScanned are useful NoSQLServer extensions, not shared database semantics.
Correct result semantics outrank a cheaper access path.
